steps.title: Take the stock
steps.text: Take a wedge (1/8 of a log) stick at least 62.27 in long. Write 1 on it in chalk.

steps.title: Rip it flush
steps.text: This piece stands taller than the frame. Rip 1.43 in off the bark side, parallel to the stick's length, so it sits flush with both faces of the panel. Lay it on a sawn face on the bandsaw or table saw; tilt the blade 22.50° (half the slice's angle) so the cut runs square to the slice's centre line.

steps.title: Cut 1 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 21.1° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the RIGHT. Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, right of the blade, is a square-ended block 3.06 in long. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 2 (first end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the raw end: 3.06 in along the point; 0.50 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 5.63 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on its mirror on the centre line: it leans 0.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Cut 3 (first end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the RIGHT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 0° (blade upright). Slide it so the blade just clears the raw end everywhere -- about 0.5 in in from the end at its longest. The offcut, left of the blade, is only a sliver. This cut meets its mirror on the centre line.

steps.title: Cut 4 (second end) on the mitre saw
steps.text: Lay the stick on the ripped face on the saw table, with the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face against the fence, the keeper to the LEFT of the blade. Mitre 34.4° — followed from the fence toward you, the cut drifts to the LEFT. Bevel 45.0° — top of the blade tilted to the LEFT. Measure from the first cut and mark: 52.61 in along the point; 61.52 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 53.99 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks across the ripped face -- the blade follows that line. The offcut, right of the blade, is a tapered piece: 16.33 in along the point, down to 9.98 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face -- keep it: it is long enough for a shorter piece. This cut meets the frame's 45° wall.

steps.title: Cut 5 (second end), marked and cut by hand
steps.text: Too steep for the mitre saw. Mark where this cut crosses each long corner, measured from the far end: 0.00 in along the point; 0.00 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face; 0.00 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face. Join the marks on every face and cut to the lines with a circular saw, bandsaw or handsaw. The cut face has to lie on its mirror on the centre line: it leans 0.0° from the panel's plane.

steps.title: Check it
steps.text: Finished: 61.52 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 53.99 in along the corner between the ripped face and the slanted sawn face, 52.61 in along the point. Measure each against the list before it goes in.

steps.title: Put it in
steps.text: It goes in as left run 1: standing on its point, bark toward the open side.

steps: Stock: split 12 in logs into eighths with the chainsaw (0.25 in kerf).
Rip flush: the standing pieces are taller than the frame; rip 1.43 in off the bark so they sit flush with both faces.
Saw settings, held as the piece lies in the panel:
18 ends: mitre 30.0°, bevel 45.0° -- the 45° wall of the long edge
18 ends: mitre 60.0°, bevel 0.0° -- meets its mirror on the centre line
Cut each piece to its long length first, then make the end cuts; measure the short length on the flat-side face to check.
fitting: Standing pieces meet the 45° slope at an angle: the first one's sawn face leans 22.5° off the slope -- plane it to suit, or start with a flipped wedge to turn the slope upright.
2 pieces near the corners are under 6 in long: cut them from offcuts.
Where a run meets a side wall at an angle, the end is a compound cut: the cut face has to lie on the 45° wall, so it is both mitred and bevelled.
